finding: Discussed five case studies of habitat loss in Benin and the Democratic Republic of the Congo, including simulated deforestation near Lubumbashi and deforestation rates against population density near Kisangani.
gap_quote: As a consequence of the pattern/process paradigm, these dynamics will have profound ecological impacts on biodiversity and ecosystem function, by means of edge effects, connectivity decline, home range reduction, and increased species mortality.

data: JAXA forest and non-forest maps for 2008 and 2016
method: driver analysis, cellular automata projection
predictors: proximity to reservoirs and roads, elevation, slope, proximity to previously deforested areas, population density
finding: Forest fell 7.29 per cent from 2008 to 2016, deforestation followed infrastructure, elevation, slope, past clearing and population, and cellular automata projected a 13.8 per cent decrease by 2030.
gap_quote: Myanmar has been experiencing a significant amount of deforestation and forest degradation in recent years.

data: not stated
method: synthetic control method
finding: Crediting baselines of 12 voluntary REDD+ projects assumed consistently higher deforestation than forest loss in synthetic control sites, so accepted methodologies overstated avoided deforestation and mitigation.
gap_quote: This requires careful consideration of whether and how much of the reduced carbon emissions can be attributed to projects. However, credible evidence on the effectiveness of such voluntary activities is limited.

data: not stated
method: spatially explicit web-based cost and benefit tool with user-defined moratorium scenarios
finding: Released REDDcalculator.com, a web tool that quantifies the carbon benefits and opportunity costs of Indonesia's forest moratorium in Kalimantan under user-defined scenarios.
gap_quote: However, it has also galvanized intense debates within Indonesian society regarding the scope of the moratorium and its consequent environmental and socioeconomic ramifications.

period: historical years not stated, projected to mid-century
data: not stated
method: spatially explicit modelling platform, not named, with deforestation scenarios
predictors: agricultural activities, internal conflict proxy, other drivers not named
finding: Agriculture drove deforestation unevenly across Colombian regions, conflict both attracted and deterred it, and mid-century trend scenarios showed major fragmentation, eased partly by enforced protected areas.
gap_quote: Understanding the causes and potential consequences of forest loss in a region, requires detailed knowledge of the spatial and temporal behavior of deforestation drivers. This is especially important in Colombia, a country with an immense geographical, ecological and cultural diversity.

data: land use data, agricultural statistics on crop areas and production
method: econometric land use choice model
predictors: road paving, other determinants not named
finding: The government road plan would cut standing forest by about 2 per cent and biological carbon by 294 teragrams, with agricultural encroachment contributing 112 teragrams.

place: pantropical, Amazon and Congo Basins, Insular Southeast Asia
data: not stated
method: relation of forest loss likelihood to fragment size, model not named
predictors: fragment size, primary forest, protected area status
finding: Loss rose as fragments shrank, mainly in primary forest and at half the rate in protected areas, while large fragments remained in the Amazon, Congo Basin and Insular Southeast Asia.
gap_quote: Results illustrate the need for rigorous land use planning, management, and enforcement in maintaining large tropical forest fragments and restoring regions of advanced fragmentation.

data: oil palm and other crop areas, source not named
method: deforestation risk models on climatic and edaphic factors, CART models
predictors: elevation, precipitation, slope, climatic and edaphic factors, distance to urban centres, roads, previously deforested areas
finding: Oil palm was under 4 per cent of cropland but 11 per cent of agricultural deforestation, 2007 to 2013, with short-term risk highest near urban centres, roads and past clearing.
gap_quote: Further expansion of agriculture in the tropics is likely to accelerate the loss of biodiversity. One crop of concern to conservation is African oil palm ( Elaeis guineensis ).

data: national deforestation data, source not named
method: Environmental Kuznets curve decomposition into scale, technique and composition effects
predictors: scale effect, technique effect, composition effect, gross domestic product
finding: Scale and composition effects were confirmed, the technique effect ran against theory, and no inverted U-shaped relation between gross domestic product and deforestation appeared in the Congo Basin.
gap_quote: These results show that there is no inverted U-shaped between gross domestic product (GDP) and deforestation in the Congo Basin as predicted in the theoretical literature.

place: Democratic Republic of the Congo, Lubumbashi charcoal production basin
data: Landsat images of 1990, 1998, 2008, 2015 and 2022
method: random forest classification, landscape ecology metrics
finding: Miombo woodland fell from 77.90 to 39.92 per cent of the basin, 1990 to 2022, mostly to grassland and wooded savannah, at almost six times the national deforestation rate.
gap_quote: Population growth in the city of Lubumbashi in the southeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DR Congo) is leading to increased energy needs, endangering the balance of the miombo woodland in the rural area referred to as the Lubumbashi charcoal production basin (LCPB).

place: Cameroon, West Region, Santchou Wildlife Reserve
data: Landsat 4-5 TM of 1988 and 2005, Landsat 8 OLI-TIRS of 2022
method: Landsat classification, CA-Markov model
validation: classification accuracy assessment, model prediction checked by agreement, reference not stated
measures: overall accuracy 89.71 to 92.24 per cent, kappa 0.87 to 0.92, prediction agreement 90.51 per cent
finding: Cultivated land grew from 158.6 to 736.4 hectares from 1988 to 2022 and was projected to reach 809.0 hectares by 2032, while mountain forest fell from 2107.4 to 1594.4 hectares.
gap_quote: Over the last three decades, the Santchou Wildlife Reserve (SWR) located in the West region of Cameroon has experienced rapid degradation.

data: not stated
method: not stated
finding: Proposed a regional network of permanent plots in Congo Basin forests to measure carbon stocks and their change, giving emission factors for national greenhouse gas inventories.
gap_quote: Pour ce faire, les pays du bassin du Congo ont besoin de développer un système de suivi des forêts fiable et opérationnel capable de mesurer les émissions et absorptions de GES liées au secteur forestier.

area: Kalimantan 538,346 square kilometres, Ketapang 12,038 square kilometres
data: Landsat time series classification
method: Landsat classification, spatially explicit oil palm expansion model with scenarios, carbon bookkeeping model, stream monitoring
finding: About 70 per cent of Kalimantan oil palm expansion cleared intact or logged forest, and plantations were projected to give 18 to 22 per cent of Indonesia's 2020 emissions.
gap_quote: Assessing ecological outcomes from major land cover transitions is therefore critical for reducing uncertainties about how food production affects the human-natural system.

place: Costa Rica, one tropical montane cloud forest site
data: historical deforestation data, Landsat time series
method: machine learning deforestation risk model, semi-structured interviews with 67 farmers, Landsat illumination analysis
predictors: topography, accessibility, other variables not named
finding: Vegetation loss was 0.14 per cent a year from 2000 to 2018, the model reached 0.89 accuracy, and PES farms and protected areas lay where predicted risk was low.
gap_quote: The development of reliable tools to predict deforestation risk is key to demonstrate efficiency and additionality when targeting protected areas or designing programs of payments for environmental services (PES).

data: observed land use data
method: deductive integrated causal model compared with inductive multinomial regression
validation: deductive model tested against observed land use, compared with a rival inductive model
measures: goodness-of-prediction 70 per cent for the deductive model, goodness-of-fit 77 per cent for the inductive model
finding: A deductive causal model predicted land use with 70 per cent goodness-of-prediction and an inductive multinomial regression fitted 77 per cent, performing equally well statistically.
gap_quote: The epistemology of virtually all these studies is inductive, searching for correlations within relatively large, sometimes spatially explicit, datasets. This can be sound science but we here aim to exemplify that there is also scope for more deductive approaches that test a pre-defined explanatory theory.

place: Ecuador, southern Ecuador mountain forest landscape
data: remote sensing data, not named
method: spatial allocation of optimised land use scenarios into deforestation projections, model not named
finding: Spatially explicit 25-year projections of forest loss under three management scenarios mapped where deforestation was most likely in the southern Ecuador mountain landscape.
gap_quote: However, providing decision-makers with reliable, site-specific data to navigate the uncertainties of forest management remains a significant challenge.

data: 33 peer-reviewed publications
method: systematic review and meta-analysis under PRISMA
predictors: rainfall, slope gradient, lithology, deforestation, mining, informal urban expansion
finding: Across 33 studies, rainfall, slope and lithology drove landslide susceptibility, deforestation and mining amplified risk, machine learning reached 88 to 92 per cent accuracy, and Central Africa remained data deficient.
gap_quote: East and North Africa exhibit the highest hazard densities due to steep terrain and high rainfall, while Central Africa remains data deficient.

place: pantropical, Amazon basin, central Africa and Southeast Asia
data: prescribed annual deforestation rates of 5, 2, 1 and 0.5 per cent
method: sensitivity analysis with the Community Climate System Model 4 with prognostic carbon and nitrogen and dynamic vegetation
finding: Deforestation rate hastened or delayed climate change, responses varied more by subcontinent, and Amazon biophysical feedbacks caused up to 55 per cent of warming and 61 per cent of drying.
gap_quote: Replication with other models is required. Although it is still unclear whether a slow but prolonged deforestation differs in impacts from one that is rapid but short, the rate can still be relevant to planning with regards to the timing of impacts.

place: Congo, eucalypt plantations, country not specified
period: the last ten years, years not stated
data: not stated
method: review of field results on belowground carbon allocation, soil CO2 efflux and carbon accretion under management options
finding: Soil carbon rose after eucalypt afforestation of savannah, rose slightly each rotation when harvest residues were left, and rose more in mixtures with nitrogen-fixing trees.
gap_quote: When they are managed on short rotations, the aboveground biomass is frequently removed and transformed into wood products with short lifetimes. The soil is thus the only compartment for durable C sequestration.

place: Republic of the Congo, production forest concessions
data: not stated
method: empirical comparison of deforestation by concession investment source, model not named
predictors: investment source, compliance with sustainable forest management policies
finding: European concessions had the highest total and core deforestation, then Asian ones, and were also most compliant with sustainable forest management, so compliance may not curb degradation.
gap_quote: Understanding how forest outcomes vary by investment source is therefore becoming increasingly important.

data: not stated
method: contextual analysis assessed against the 3E+ criteria of effectiveness, efficiency, equity and co-benefits
finding: Described the context for REDD+ in Cameroon, covering drivers of deforestation, institutions, revenue sharing, political economy and actors, and assessed its REDD+ profile against the 3E+ criteria.

place: Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kahuzi-Biega National Park landscape
data: Landsat tropical moist forest data of Vancutsem et al. 2021, spatial driver datasets
method: meshing, multi-scale analysis, principal component analysis, zoning, multiple linear regression, bootstrapped relative importance
predictors: fire, other spatial drivers not named
finding: Edge and outer zones lost about 30 per cent of forest from 1990 to 2022, the inner zone stayed stable, and fire was the most influential driver.
gap_quote: The protected areas (PA) of the Democratic Republic of the Congo serve as vital carbon reservoirs and are crucial for biodiversity conservation and climate regulation. Despite their significance, these areas face escalating rates of deforestation and degradation, often poorly understood at the local level.

data: future land use trajectories under scenarios, product not named
method: overlay of projected land use trajectories on protection levels across biomes, correlation analysis
finding: Projected loss of primary vegetation showed no significant correlation with protection extent, and Central African tropical forests and boreal forests had the most projected change with low protection.
gap_quote: Tropical Forests in Central Africa and the Boreal Forests of North Euro-Asia and Canada emerge as the areas where most projected change occurs, and existing protection is still low.

data: Landsat TM and ETM+ of 1986, 2000 and 2008, GPS ground reference points
method: Landsat land cover classification, household questionnaires and focus groups, tree damage plots
predictors: agricultural expansion, illegal logging, fuel wood collection, household size
validation: ground reference data from GPS points, accuracy not stated
finding: Deforestation ran at 1.09 per cent a year from 1986 to 2000 and 0.58 per cent from 2001 to 2008, and farming fires damaged 460 trees of 98 species.
gap_quote: Massive tree destruction was recorded due to land use changes specifically agricultural expansions, illegal logging and fuel wood collection with consequent threats to forest biodiversity.

data: FAO land use and land cover and projected changes
method: Liverpool Malaria Model driven by bias-corrected REMO ensemble runs, MARA Seasonality Model, Garki model
predictors: daily mean temperature, 10-day accumulated precipitation, FAO land use and land cover change through the climate model
validation: calibration and validation against surveyed entomological and parasitological values, comparison with the original model
finding: Projected warming and drying, largely from land surface degradation, would cut malaria transmission in the Sahel, delay seasons farther south and extend malaria in East African highlands by 2050.
gap_quote: The projected climate change will probably alter the range and transmission potential of malaria in Africa.

period: plan horizon 2039, data years not stated
data: not stated
method: household survey of 85 heads, diagnostic analysis, case studies and scenarios, urban master plan
finding: Proposed a 2039 urban master plan zoning Mongoumba to reconcile urban growth, farming and forest protection as the Corridor 13 road and port raise deforestation risk.
gap_quote: Mongoumba, ville forestière située dans le bassin du Congo, au sud-ouest de la République Centrafricaine, est confrontée à une déforestation accélérée, principalement due à l’agriculture sur brûlis.

place: Brazil, Peru, Cameroon, Tanzania, Indonesia and Vietnam, 130 villages
data: household survey data on reported forest clearing
method: comparison of household outcomes across REDD+ intervention types at two times, model not named
finding: Disincentives alone lowered perceived tenure security and well-being, incentives eased the well-being loss, and in Brazil disincentives cut reported forest clearing but hurt well-being most.
gap_quote: Although safeguards represent a key step for promoting social responsibility in REDD+, they are challenging to operationalize and monitor.

data: global remote sensing deforestation and carbon stock products, not named
method: comparison of deforestation and carbon stock products and derived emission estimates
finding: Deforestation estimates from global Earth observation products disagreed strikingly in Guinea-Bissau, driving high uncertainty in emissions, while carbon stock datasets agreed better and added little variation.
gap_quote: Developing these baselines requires accurate maps of carbon stocks and historical deforestation. Global remote sensing products provide low-cost solutions for this information, but there has been little validation of these products at national scales.

data: GIS layers for key crops, sources not named
method: von Thünen land rent model with GIS mapping, conceptual framework
finding: Intensifying key crops in the Democratic Republic of the Congo would raise land rents and so conservation costs, which could exceed current and projected carbon credit prices.
gap_quote: However, underlying assumptions remain uncertain and have been little explored in the context of conservation incentive schemes such as policies for Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and forest Degradation, conservation, sustainable management, and enhancement of carbon stocks (REDD+).

place: Cameroon, Momo Division, Ajei forest area
data: Landsat 1986 and 2020, ASTER 2003, 2007 and 2020
method: descriptive analysis of questionnaires, focus groups, interviews and satellite images
predictors: agriculture, population growth, settlement, knowledge of conservation, accessibility, knowledge of deforestation
finding: Agriculture, 37.4 per cent, and population growth, 31.3 per cent, were the main drivers of land use patterns, ahead of settlement and accessibility, amid topographic, institutional and socio-economic constraints.
gap_quote: Owing to this relationship, most salient consequences trigger disconnects between man and ecological services.

data: historical land use and land cover data derived by the study
method: linear and non-linear deforestation baselines, IPCC Tier 2 look-up method, Tier 3 regression of carbon storage
finding: Eastern Tanzania stored 1.58 petagrams of aboveground live carbon in 2000 by Tier 2 and 1.32 by Tier 3, with 0.94 petagrams committed release from 1908 to 2000.
gap_quote: Thus, the success of climate change policy developments such as REDD+ (Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation) relies heavily on measuring and understanding this variation in the past, present and future.

data: not stated
method: Geographic Emission Benchmark land change model, compared with GEOMOD
validation: compared with GEOMOD, a rival model
measures: Figure of Merit, value not stated
finding: Proposed the Geographic Emission Benchmark model for reference level activity data, whose projection in the Chinese tropics was more accurate than GEOMOD by Figure of Merit.

period: training years not stated, forecasts for 2016 to 2018
data: past deforestation maps, product not named, other covariates
method: spatio-temporal ConvLSTM deep learning model
predictors: past deforestation, other covariates not named
validation: later years held out, one to three years ahead
finding: A ConvLSTM model forecast Amazon deforestation one year ahead with an F1 score of 0.47, improving on prior work, with promising results within three years and limits beyond.
gap_quote: Reducing tropical deforestation effectively requires spatially explicit data on deforestation dynamics. While past deforestation is now detected and mapped with high accuracy, producing reliable future forecasts remains a challenge.
